title: The Testing Methods Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Testing is the discipline of executing a system to find where it breaks and proving where it holds. It spans software testing (unit, integration, system, acceptance), hardware testing (bed-of-nails, boundary scan, environmental stress), and engineering verification (reviews, inspections, analysis). Good testing is planned before code is written: a test plan names what is in scope, a test case names exact inputs and expected outputs, and a test report names what actually happened. This database records the methods, the frameworks that automate them, the tools that measure them, and the verification methods that prove the system meets its requirements.
capabilities: Testing levels: unit, integration, system, acceptance — what each proves
Test plan anatomy: scope, schedule, resources, entry and exit criteria
Test case anatomy: preconditions, inputs, steps, expected results
Verification vs validation: building it right vs building the right thing
Coverage thinking: statement, branch, and requirements coverage

title: The Testing Methods Database — Unit testing with the xUnit family
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Unit testing exercises the smallest testable part of software — usually one function or class — in isolation. The xUnit family (JUnit for Java, NUnit for .NET, pytest and unittest for Python) shares one pattern: arrange, act, assert. Arrange sets up inputs and doubles, act calls the unit under test, assert checks the result against the expectation. Good unit tests are fast, independent, repeatable, and readable; they run on every commit so regressions are caught within minutes. Mocks and stubs replace collaborators the unit does not own, and code coverage tools report which lines the tests actually executed.
capabilities: Arrange-act-assert pattern with worked examples
Test doubles: mocks, stubs, fakes, spies — when each is honest
Coverage tools: statement and branch coverage reporting
Running tests in CI: fail-fast pipelines on every commit

title: The Testing Methods Database — Integration and system testing
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Integration testing proves that modules work together: top-down integration starts at the user-facing layer and stubs what is below, bottom-up starts at the data layer and drivers what is above, and big-bang wires everything at once. System testing then treats the whole assembly as a black box and checks functional behavior, performance under load, security posture, and recovery from failure. A system test environment mirrors production as closely as budget allows — same operating system, same database version, realistic data volumes — because bugs that only appear at scale are the expensive ones.
capabilities: Top-down, bottom-up, and big-bang integration strategies
Interface contracts: what each module promises its neighbors
System test environments that mirror production
Non-functional testing: load, stress, soak, and spike tests

title: The Testing Methods Database — Test planning in the IEEE 829 style
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. A test plan written in the IEEE 829 tradition names the test items, the features to be tested and those explicitly out of scope, the approach, the pass and fail criteria, the suspension and resumption rules, the deliverables, the schedule, and the risks. Entry criteria say when testing may begin (code complete, environment ready); exit criteria say when it may stop (all planned cases run, defect thresholds met, coverage targets hit). Risk-based planning spends the most effort where failure hurts most: payment code gets more tests than the about page. The plan is a living record — it is revised when scope changes, and the final test report compares plan against reality.
capabilities: IEEE 829 test plan sections with a filled example
Entry and exit criteria templates
Risk-based prioritization of test effort
Test reporting: planned vs executed vs passed

title: The Testing Methods Database — Test case design techniques
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Test case design turns requirements into the smallest set of cases that still finds the bugs. Equivalence partitioning splits inputs into classes that should behave the same and tests one representative of each; boundary value analysis tests the edges where off-by-one errors hide (for a range of 1 to 100: 0, 1, 2, 99, 100, 101). Decision tables map combinations of conditions to actions for business rules; state transition testing walks every legal and illegal move between states. Pairwise testing covers every pair of parameter values when full combinations would explode. Each technique is a different lens — strong suites combine several.
capabilities: Equivalence partitioning with worked classes
Boundary value analysis: the edge values that catch off-by-one bugs
Decision tables for business-rule combinations
State transition diagrams and illegal-transition tests

title: The Testing Methods Database — Test automation frameworks
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Automation frameworks turn repeatable checks into code that runs unattended. Selenium drives real browsers through WebDriver, Playwright adds auto-waiting and multi-browser support, and Cypress runs inside the browser for fast front-end tests. The page-object model keeps tests maintainable by putting selectors and actions in one class per page instead of scattering them through every test. Good automation suites run in continuous integration: every pull request triggers the suite, failures block the merge, and flaky tests are quarantined rather than ignored. Automation checks regressions; it does not replace exploratory testing by a thinking human.
capabilities: Selenium, Playwright, and Cypress compared honestly
Page-object model for maintainable UI tests
CI pipelines: running suites on every pull request
Flaky test quarantine and retry policy records

title: The Testing Methods Database — Hardware and embedded testing
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Hardware testing proves physical things. Bed-of-nails fixtures press spring-loaded probes onto every test point of a circuit board; JTAG boundary scan shifts test patterns through chips to find solder faults without probes; in-circuit testers check component values on assembled boards. Hardware-in-the-loop rigs run real embedded firmware against simulated sensors and actuators so control software is tested before the machine exists. Environmental stress screening bakes, shakes, and freezes products (thermal cycling, vibration, humidity) to force infant-mortality failures in the factory instead of in the customer's hands.
capabilities: Bed-of-nails and in-circuit test fixtures
JTAG boundary scan for solder and interconnect faults
Hardware-in-the-loop rigs for embedded firmware
Environmental stress: thermal, vibration, humidity screening

title: The Testing Methods Database — Verification and validation methods
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Verification asks "are we building the product right" and validation asks "are we building the right product." Reviews and inspections catch defects in documents and code before anything runs — a formal inspection with a checklist routinely finds more defects per hour than testing does. Static analysis tools scan code for bug patterns, unused variables, and security flaws without executing it. Traceability matrices link every requirement to the test cases that prove it, so no requirement ships untested and no test exists without a reason. Independent verification teams, separate from the builders, bring fresh eyes to safety-critical systems.
capabilities: Reviews vs inspections: formal defect-hunting checklists
Static analysis tools and the bug patterns they catch
Traceability matrices: requirement to test case to result
Independent verification for safety-critical systems
